capabilities.target: payments-agent pay_vendor task carrying chosen vendor and bank details

inputs.source: Employee purchase request, SSO authenticated, manager-approved on item and budget before any quote exists
Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders
payments-agent A2A agent card, fetched at startup, unsigned and unpinned

instructions.note: 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote' binds payment destination to whatever appears in the inbound email with no verification against a stored, known-good bank account for the vendor.
'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks' assumes a downstream safety net that the runtime notes contradict: payments-agent pays the bank details in the task with no additional verification.

Manager approval of the purchase request (item/budget, given before any quote exists) is treated by the design as authorizing the eventual specific payment, but that approval record is never passed to payments-agent.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: Human approval is enforced outside the model and does not decay with capability, but it only covers the initial item/budget decision, made before any vendor quote or bank detail exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent, so it never gates the actual payment action.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: only pay vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends on the model checking the vendor name against the approved list. As written, the check never extends to bank account details, so a spoofed or compromised quote sent under an approved vendor's name with fraudulent bank details passes this check regardless of model capability. This is a design gap, not just a capability-driven bypass, so no additional capability makes this control weaker or stronger.

controls.name: Payment destination confirmation bound to vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: Would validate the bank account in any payment task against a previously stored, verified value for the approved vendor rather than trusting the value found in an inbound email, closing the substitution path under any model behavior.

controls.name: Bind and propagate approval context to payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Would require payments-agent to verify that a human-approved record matches the specific vendor, amount, and bank details being paid, before executing, closing the authority laundering gap regardless of orchestrator behavior.

controls.name: Sign and pin payments-agent's agent card and skill definitions
controls.decay_rationale: Would prevent an unauthenticated or altered agent card from being trusted at startup or thereafter, closing spoofing and rug-pull paths regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted vendor quote bank details flow directly into irreversible A2A payment delegation

attack_path.note: External email contains a quote and bank details; sender and content are not authenticated.
Agent confirms the vendor name appears on the approved list (name-only check).
Agent delegates a pay_vendor task to payments-agent using bank details taken verbatim from the email; payments-agent pays them with no further check.

evidence.observation: payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
'Use the bank details from the chosen quote. Only pay vendors on the approved list.' binds payment destination to unvalidated email content and checks only vendor name, not bank account.
Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.

recommendations.action: Bind the payment destination to a verified, previously-stored bank account per approved vendor; reject any payment task whose bank details differ from the system of record, regardless of quote content.
Require payments-agent to independently validate payment destination rather than trusting orchestrator-supplied task details wholesale.

findings.title: Authority laundering (TC7): manager approval does not cover or propagate to the irreversible payment delegation

attack_path.note: Manager approves budget/item before any vendor or bank detail is known.
Approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
Payment proceeds on payments-agent's unconditional trust of the orchestrator's token, with no verification that a human approved this specific vendor, amount, or destination.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
Authentication is a single bearer scheme with no per-task or per-approval binding.

recommendations.action: Propagate a signed approval record (vendor, amount, destination) from the manager approval step through to payments-agent; have payments-agent refuse to pay unless the task matches an approval record.
Log and alert whenever a payment delegation's vendor or bank details differ from anything present at approval time.

findings.title: Agentic supply chain gap (ASI04): payments-agent's agent card is unsigned, unpinned, and unverified

attack_path.note: Agent card fetched at startup over an unauthenticated channel, no signature or pin.
Orchestrator relies on the fetched card's skill description to invoke pay_vendor and trusts it unconditionally.

evidence.observation: The card carries no signature field and authentication is limited to a bearer scheme.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Pin or hash payments-agent's agent card and skill definitions; refuse to operate if the fetched card does not match the pinned version.
Verify payments-agent's identity (mTLS or signed identity) rather than relying on a static bearer token and URL alone.

rating.rationale: Three findings were identified, all with horizon present. F1 (untrusted vendor email bank details flowing into an irreversible A2A payment) and F3 (unsigned, unpinned payments-agent card) both reach inherent and residual critical: source class is untrusted or unknown, the sink is an irreversible, egress-carrying delegate action, and no credited control narrows or severs either path. The only declared preventive controls -- a pre-quote manager approval (ctl.manager_approval) and a prompt instruction restricting payment to approved vendor names (ctl.vendor_allowlist_instruction) -- do not cover the specific attribute being exploited (the bank account destination) and so earn no tier credit under the rubric. F2 (authority laundering, the approval covering budget/item but never propagating to the specific payment) reaches high. Because none of the present-day controls are actually credited against these paths, the forecast equals the residual: there is no further degradation available from a future trigger, since the controls that would decay under model_upgrade or autonomy_increase (the vendor-allowlist instruction, the pre-quote approval) already provide no protection for the dimension attackers would use. The single highest-leverage fix is ctl.destination_confirmation: binding payment destination to a stored, verified vendor bank record instead of the value in an inbound email or task, which would sever F1 and materially reduce F2 and F3.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/A2A wire-level configuration, IaC, or source code was available; credential scope and the exact authentication flow for payments-agent's bearer token are inferred from the runtime notes and scored as shared_service_account with medium-to-high confidence.

The contents of the approved vendor list were not provided; it is assessed as a name-only list (no stored bank account reference) based on the description given, which is the basis for finding f1. If the list in fact stores verified bank details that are checked, f1's residual risk would be lower and this should be re-verified against the actual implementation.
